items.title: Randy Sandke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: I was doing a concert opposite Lionel Hampton and Lionel Hampton said, he got to the microphone and he said, “Benny Goodman was the Abraham Lincoln of jazz. If it wasn’t for him I wouldn’t be here doing as well as I am.”

ctx.x: Yeah okay. But I mean it’s like an irony. See like you got me going now. But an irony. Now take Benny Goodman, who was really until recently known for this guy who broke the color barrier. He was the guy that hired Lionel Hampton and Teddy Wilson and he was, like with Benny Goodman died, that week I was doing a concert opposite Lionel Hampton and Lionel Hampton said, he got to the microphone and he said, “Benny Goodman was the Abraham Lincoln of jazz. If it wasn’t for him I wouldn’t be here doing as well as I…

guys were able to get their music out. And artistically they were not stymied. Today I think it’s a little different because I just feel like certain people are just not being allowed to express themselves because of a racial thing that really it wasn’t. People want to think that it was that way back then with Duke and Louis Armstrong, but it wasn’t.
